 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE,                       §            OF
 MASON                                           §
 IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,                        §
 CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO,                       §
 MASON, MCCULLOCH,                               §

 GREEN AND WILLIAMSON                            §    ADMINISTRATIVE
 COUNTIES                                        §      HEARINGS




                              E6 LINK INTERVENORS’
                               POST HEARING BRIEF


TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE JUDGES

      COME NOW the E6 Link Intervenors, and pursuant to SOAH order No.’s 6 and

31 file this Post-Hearing Reply Brief for the aligned E6 Link Intervenors and would

respectfully show the Court the following:




                                             1
  I.       SUPPORT FOR THE BEST-MEETS ROUTE 894, THE COMMISSION STAFF
                     PREFERRED ROUTE, OR ROUTE CCG

      A. Route 894 Satisfies the Statutory Routing Criteria.

         1.     Route 894 was identified by the Joint Applicants as the best-meets route and

remains the route that most appropriately balances the routing criteria contained in

PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC § 25.101. The record demonstrates that Route 894 minimizes

impacts to habitable structures and avoids Links E6 and E12, the two links with the

highest habitable structure counts in the record.

         2.     Numerous witnesses testified that prudent avoidance requires the

Commission to minimize impacts to existing residences whenever reasonably possible.

Route 894 contains 85 habitable structures. By contrast, Solana's preferred Route 392

utilizes Link E12, the second most populated link in the record, and contains 136

habitable structures, while Solana's other proposed Route 402 utilizes Link E6, the most

populated link in the record, and contains 169 habitable structures. Selecting Route 392

would increase residential impacts by approximately 60%, while selecting Route 402

would nearly double them. Because Route 894 accomplishes the Project's purpose while

avoiding those substantial additional impacts, it best satisfies the Commission's routing

criteria and should be selected.

      B. The Commission Staff’s Preferred Route Satisfies the Statutory Routing Criteria.

         3.      Commission Staff independently evaluated the proposed routes and

concluded that Route 487 is the best route when weighing the factors set forth in PURA

                                              2
 § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). Staff specifically recommended Route 487

rather than the Joint Applicants' best-meets Route 894.

       4.     In support of that recommendation, Staff testified that Route 487 would

mitigate concerns expressed by affected landowners and intervenors. Staff noted that

Route 487 contains only 96 habitable structures and specifically emphasized that it does

not utilize Link E6, which contains the highest number of habitable structures within 500

feet of the centerline of any proposed link in the record.

       5.     Staff’s selected Route 487 and the Joint Applicants selected Route 894 are

substantially similar and both avoid Links E6 and E12, the two most heavily populated

links in the record. That shared conclusion weighs strongly against selecting Solana's

proposed routes, which rely on those same links.

   C. Route CCG Provides Additional Support for Avoiding Links E6 and E12.

       6.     Expert witness Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke concluded that Route CCG

best satisfies the routing criteria contained in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B). Reinecke testified that Route CCG follows Route 894 where Route 894

performs well while making targeted modifications to improve environmental, land use,

and community value considerations.

       7.     Reinecke specifically evaluated routing alternatives utilizing Links E6 and

E12 and determined that the resulting increase in impacts to habitable structures was not

a balanced or justified tradeoff. In comparing Route CCG's eastern routing sequence to



                                             3
 an alternative utilizing Link E12, Reinecke found that the E12 alternative would place

substantially more habitable structures in close proximity to the transmission line.

Accordingly, she recommended a routing sequence that avoids both Links E6 and E12.

         8.      Route CCG therefore provides additional support for the conclusion

reached by both the Joint Applicants and Commission Staff — the Project can be routed

successfully without utilizing Links E6 or E12.

   II.         PUBLIC HEALTH CONSIDERATIONS SUPPORT AVOIDING ROUTES
                   THAT IMPACT THE GREATES NUMBER OF HOMES.

         9.      Dr. David O. Carpenter testified on behalf of the E6 Link Intervenors. Dr.

Carpenter is a public health physician and environmental health scientist, the Vincent

O'Leary Professor of Environmental Health Sciences at the University at Albany, and Co-

Director of the Institute for Health and the Environment, a World Health Organization

Collaborating Centre. He attended Harvard University and Harvard Medical School,

authored more than 500 peer-reviewed publications, served as Executive Secretary of the

New York State Power Lines Project, and testified before both the President's Cancer

Panel and the United States House of Representatives regarding EMF exposure and

cancer risks. E6 Link Intervenors Exhibit 39.

         10.     Based on his education, training, research, and review of the scientific

literature, Dr. Carpenter testified that substantial scientific literature discusses potential

associations between prolonged EMF exposure and adverse health effects, including

childhood leukemia and other health conditions. He further testified that prudent public

                                              4
 health policy supports minimizing unnecessary EMF exposure where reasonably feasible

alternatives exist and that the number of residences located near a transmission line route

is an important public health consideration. E6 Link Intervenors Exhibit 39.

   III. THE COMMISSION SHOULD NOT INCREASE IMPACTS TO EXISTING
           RESIDENTS TO ACCOMMODATE A FUTURE DEVELOPMENT.

   A. Solana’s Proposal Would Shift Significant Impacts onto Existing Landowners.

       11.    The impacts associated with Solana's preferred routes, or any route

utilizing Link E6, are not theoretical. They would directly affect existing landowners and

families who live along the proposed route.

       12.    The Campbell family property and the neighboring properties provide just

one example of the impacts associated with Link E6. Within this relatively short section

of the route, the proposed transmission line would run directly through the Campbell

family's hay field while also being located immediately adjacent to the homes of 43

noticed landowners along Spring Creek Loop.




                                              5
                                                         E6 Link Intervenors Exhibit 42.

       13.    The White family property provides another example of the impacts

associated with Link E6. The proposed route would pass immediately adjacent to the

property's only entrance and would affect land maintained under a Wildlife Management

designation through habitat preservation and wildlife conservation efforts. The result

would be a direct impact on both the family's access to their home and the long-term use

of their property.




                                                        E6 Link Intervenors Exhibit 36.

       14.    The Cabaniss family properties, consisting of Oncor tract numbers 5518,

5518.1, 5520, and 5519, provide another example of the impacts associated with Link E6.




                                           6
 The proposed route divides a long-held family tract and passes in close proximity to

several existing residences. Most notably, the route would be located virtually on top of

one of the homes situated on the property. The Commission should not impose such a

direct impact on an existing residence when reasonable alternatives are available.




                                                            E6 Link Intervenor Exhibit 4.

      15.    The Commission should be particularly hesitant to increase impacts to

existing agricultural and residential properties where the admitted purpose is to avoid

additional cost and inconvenience to a development that has not yet broken ground. The

record demonstrates that Solana’s state of the art experts can continue developing their

property regardless of the transmission line. Existing landowners, however, do not have

the same ability to redesign their properties around the Project.

   B. The Record Demonstrates that these Impacts Extend to Property Values.




                                            7
       16.    The impacts to existing landowners are not limited to the physical

placement of a transmission line. The record also contains expert testimony regarding the

effect high-voltage transmission lines can have on property values.

      17.    Scott R. Lucas, MAI, a Certified General Real Estate Appraiser with more

than twenty years of appraisal experience in Texas, testified that properties affected by

high-voltage transmission lines and related easements can and do experience diminished

market value when compared to similar unaffected properties. Mr. Lucas has performed

numerous appraisals involving transmission line easements and reviewed multiple case

studies involving properties impacted by high-voltage transmission facilities.

      18.    Mr. Lucas testified that case studies involving properties affected by high-

voltage transmission lines showed diminution in value ranging from 2% to 61%. He

further noted that many of those examples involved transmission lines of lower voltage

and easements of lesser width than the 765-kV transmission line proposed in this

proceeding. E6 Link Intervenors Exhibit 38.

   C. Solana's Development Can Proceed Without Shifting Greater Impacts to Existing
      Residents.

      19.    Solana urges the Commission to route the Project in a manner that avoids

impacts to its planned residential development. However, the development has not been

constructed and has not broken ground.

      20.    The record demonstrates that the transmission line does not prevent Solana

from developing its property. To the contrary, Solana's own witness testified that its

                                           8
 experienced team of engineers and developers could design around the transmission line

and continue developing the project. The primary consequence identified by Solana was

additional time, expense, and development challenges.

       21.       Existing residents do not have the same flexibility. Unlike Solana, they

cannot redesign their homes, relocate their neighborhoods, or move existing agricultural

operations. The Commission's rules define "habitable structures" as structures "normally

inhabited by humans or intended to be inhabited by humans on a daily or regular basis."

16 TAC § 25.101(a)(3). Consistent with that focus, the Commission should not increase

impacts to existing homes and communities in order to avoid impacts to homes that do

not yet exist.

       22.       Nevertheless, Solana asks the Commission to select Route 392 or Route 402.

Those routes contain 136 and 169 habitable structures, respectively, and utilize Links E12

and E6 — the second and first most populated links in the record. Additional cost and

delay to a future development do not justify imposing greater impacts on families who

already live along the proposed route.

                                   IV.    CONCLUSION

       23.       The record demonstrates that the Project can be successfully routed

without utilizing either Link E6 or Link E12. Route 894, Route 487, and Route CCG all

avoid the substantial impacts associated with the two most heavily populated links in the

record while still satisfying the Project's objectives.



                                               9
        24.    The Commission should not increase impacts to existing residents, homes,

farms, and family properties in order to accommodate a future development that has not

yet been constructed. For these reasons, the E6 Link Intervenors respectfully request that

the Administrative Law Judges recommend a route that avoids Links E6 and E12 and

reject routes utilizing those links.




                                                Respectfully submitted,

                                                GRISSOM & THOMPSON, L.L.P
